definition: Cache-aside reads the database on a cache miss and places the result in the cache.
A cache hit finds the requested unexpired value in the cache.
A cache miss occurs when a requested value is absent or expired.
A time to live specifies how long a cached value remains valid before expiration.
Write-through updates the cache when the application writes data to its database.
A shard holds part of a Valkey or Redis OSS dataset with a primary and optional replicas.
A read replica holds a copy of primary data and serves read requests.
Replication lag is the delay between changes at a primary and their arrival at a replica.
An endpoint is the address an application uses to connect to a cache node or cluster.
A subnet group identifies the VPC subnets eligible to host node-based cache nodes.
RBAC assigns cache users permissions for particular commands and keys.
A transactional log durably records changes across Availability Zones for recovery.
Asynchronous replication copies primary updates to secondary clusters without waiting for those copies before continuing.
An Availability Zone is a separate placement location within an AWS Region used to isolate failures.
